summary: Creates an IANA registry for the flags in the Prefix Information Option of IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Router Advertisements. Two flags were defined and six bits were left reserved, and another RFC had already used a flag without any registry existing. This document fixes that gap and updates RFC 4861.

plainLanguage.summary: A club had a list of badge colors but nobody kept an official list. This starts the official list so no two people pick the same color by accident.

questions: ipv6 prefix information option flags registry
iana registry for router advertisement flags
subtitle: Creating a registry for IPv6 router advertisement flag definitions.

tldr.problem: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery's Prefix Information Option had flags defined in multiple RFCs, but no IANA registry to manage them and prevent collisions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8425 creates an IANA registry for Prefix Information Option flags, documents the existing three flags, and specifies that new flags require Standards Action.
tldr.outcome: PIO flags are now centrally managed, preventing conflicts and enabling future IPv6 extensions.

today: RFC 8425 is a Proposed Standard. The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Prefix Information Option Flags registry remains the central source for PIO flag definitions.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The Prefix Information Option (PIO) in IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Router Advertisement messages contains an 8-bit flag field. RFC 4861 originally defined two flags: the On-link Flag (L) and the Autonomous Address Configuration Flag (A). Later, RFC 6275 added the Router Address Flag (R) without creating an IANA registry. When multiple RFCs started defining flags in the same field without coordination, it became clear that a registry was needed to prevent conflicts.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers send messages with a set of on/off switches for different behaviors. Different RFCs had been flipping switches without keeping score.

sections.title: The Three Flags
sections.content: The Prefix Information Option flag field has three flags currently defined: the L flag (bit 0) indicates that the prefix is on-link, the A flag (bit 1) enables autonomous address configuration, and the R flag (bit 2) indicates that the prefix should be used for the Router Address. The remaining 5 bits (bits 3-7) are reserved.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three switches already defined. Six more switches are set aside for future use.

sections.title: Registry Creation
sections.content: RFC 8425 creates the IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Prefix Information Option Flags registry at IANA. The registry lists the current three flags and documents the reserved bits. New flags can only be added through the Standards Action process, meaning they must be defined in a published RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA now keeps an official notebook listing all the switches and which ones are reserved for future use.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 8425 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4861. The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery Prefix Information Option Flags registry is maintained by IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: This is the official rule for managing the on/off switches in IPv6 router messages.
